v.3: by the Even and the Odd,
v.4: by the night when it departs!
v.5: Is there an oath in that for one possessing intellect?
v.6: Have you not regarded how your Lord dealt with [the people of] ‘Ad,
v.8: the like of which was not created among cities,
v.9: and [the people of] Thamud, who hollowed out the rocks in the valley,
v.11: —those who rebelled [against Allah] in their cities
v.12: and caused much corruption in them,
v.13: so your Lord poured on them lashes of punishment.
v.14: Indeed your Lord is in ambush.
v.15: As for man, whenever his Lord tests him, and grants him honour, and blesses him, he says, ‘My Lord has honoured me.’
v.16: But when He tests him and tightens for him his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’
v.17: No indeed! No, you do not honour the orphan,
v.18: and do not urge the feeding of the needy.
v.20: and love wealth with much fondness.
v.21: No indeed! When the earth is levelled to a plain,
v.22: and your Lord [’s edict] arrives with the angels in ranks,
v.23: the day when hell is brought [near], man will take admonition on that day, but what will that admonition avail him?
v.24: He will say, ‘Alas, had I sent ahead for my life [in the Hereafter]!’
v.25: On that day none shall punish as He punishes,
v.26: and none shall bind as He binds.
v.28: Return to your Lord, pleased and pleasing!
